Tim Shipman has written about what will be coming up at the Labour conference next week in his cover story for the Spectator. He says:

Labour special advisers summoned last week to the pillared state room on the first floor of No. 10 to hear the plan for conference from Burnham’s political secretary, Hayden Munro, left in no doubt that the PM wants to be a transformational figure. The conference ‘narrative’ these advisers were urged to push includes the telling line: ‘This Labour government will bring forward the biggest change to Britain in 40 years, with a new political and economic model.’ On the specifics, Burnham will pledge: ‘We will make the choices that are needed to end rough sleeping, solve the social care crisis and get more young people into work.’

Burnham will pledge to run a ‘cost-of-living government’ with further ‘immediate action’ to ‘provide the breathing space people need’, as well as outline plans to devolve power ‘out of Whitehall’, ‘reindustrialise Britain’ and take back public control of ‘the essentials in life – such as energy, water and housing’ to ‘make them affordable again’.

Ultimately, the election choice is Burnham’s. ‘If you knew what Keir’s aides thought, you knew what he would do,’ says a ministerial aide. ‘But Andy has political opinions of his own.’ Burnham may go for it. But those closest to him doubt it. ‘He likes risk, but he has stuff he wants to get done,’ says one close confidant. While outsiders think his ambitions require an election, Burnham thinks he can transform Britain without one. ‘Andy really cares about the devolution stuff,’ the ministerial aide observes. ‘Most of Westminster roll their eyes but he thinks that will change the country. He thinks doing that will make him a great prime minister.’

And those who think none of that will deal with Britain’s economic problems seize on another clue. A Labour adviser concludes: ‘Ultimately I think Burnham and his team will do what they often do with difficult decisions, and not make one.’

What I imagine is that some schools will offer some of these subjects where their local labour market demands, and this is where our mayors and our local leaders are really helping to shape that in their area.

So I wouldn’t expect a school to offer all of these, as they don’t offer all GCSEs at the moment. They will specialise in particular areas.

If you’re trying to do engineering or construction, for example, you know that involves a lot of problem solving, a lot of maths, a lot of thinking, as well as the hands-on skills that’s required.

So it’s not dumbing down, it’s the opposite of that, actually, because this is about raising the standards and the rigour and regulating these qualifications.

As they sit down to a White House dinner hours after news that OpenAI had hacked the Australian government, we’ll ask who will call to task the US tech titans at the table.

events.title: Residents in West Bank's Masafer Yatta face Israeli demolitions

events.title: How do the French feel about religion?

events.title: 'Trump views US-China relations as a personal friendship: Xi views US as an adversary to be managed'
events.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Henrietta Levin, Senior Fellow with the Freeman Chair in China Studies at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington. Levin warns that President Trump’s highly personalized approach to Xi Jinping offers Beijing opportunities that China can easily exploit. Xi does not approach the relationship in the same way. events.title: 8 service members attempted suicide on USS Lincoln during extended deployment, Navy says
events.summary: The ship, which supported the U.S. war with Iran, was at sea for nearly 300 days without a port call.

events.title: Ex-boyfriend of former Sen. Kyrsten Sinema allegedly threw 22 of her paintings in a pool
events.summary: Former Arizona Sen. Kyrsten Sinema’s former bodyguard and romantic partner was arrested earlier this month in Maricopa County after allegedly breaking into her home and damaging $200,000 worth of artwork and expensive alcohol.

events.title: Federal authorities investigating attorney, accountant linked to Epstein’s estate, source says
events.summary: The lawyer, Darren Indyke, and the accountant, Richard Kahn, are administrators and executors of Jeffrey Epstein’s estate.

events.title: ‘Fed up with a war they didn't want’: Midwestern voters air frustrations impacting the midterms
events.summary: Senior National Politics Reporter Jonathan Allen joins Meet the Press NOW to discuss his conversations with frustrated voters on the ground in Iowa and Ohio ahead of the midterms in his Drive to Decision Day series.

events.title: Trump welcomes Xi for a White House summit set to be high on pageantry, low on substance
events.summary: Both the U.S. and Chinese leaders are seeking to maintain stability in ties between the world’s two biggest economies, with few concrete results expected from their White House meeting.

events.title: Netanyahu defends Iran war, calls Gaza genocide accusations a lie in defiant U.N. address
events.summary: As Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case at the United Nations General Assembly, his target audience will likely be Israeli voters.

events.title: Senate rejects resolution calling to end the Iran war, as most Republicans stick with Trump
events.summary: The Senate voted to direct President Donald Trump to end the U.S. war with Iran, after several Republicans defected and voted with Democrats.

events.title: Iran’s president says Tehran wants a deal with U.S. before midterm elections
events.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday suggested his government was willing to make a deal with the U.S. to end the war before Americans head to the polls this November.

events.title: Graphic: Tracking ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has been at a near-standstill for weeks amid the Iran war, sending prices of oil and other key goods soaring.

events.title: Map: See how gas prices have changed in the county where you live
events.summary: How much gas prices have increased during the Iran war depends entirely on where you live, an NBC News analysis of average gas price data from AAA shows.

events.title: White House still turning away some media outlets despite order
events.summary: Some journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are being denied entry to the White House despite a judge ordering that their access be restored. The ongoing legal battle over the media ban and suspension of the White House TV pool are changing how the public sees President Trump’s historic meeting with Chinese President Xi.

events.title: Hurricane Polo fuels fears of heavy rain and landslides in Mexico’s southwest
events.summary: Southwestern Mexico is bracing for heavy rain and mudslides after Polo, a powerful Pacific cyclone, intensified into a major hurricane.

events.title: Cuban foreign minister addresses talks with U.S., blackouts
events.summary: NBC News' Andrea Mitchell sat down with Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla to discuss President Trump's speech at the United Nations, whether Cuba has been in talks with the U.S., and blackouts in the country.

events.title: Trump hosts China’s leader at high-stakes summit
events.summary: President Trump is hosting China’s leader Xi Jinping for a high-stakes summit in Washington. NBC News’ Gabe Gutierrez reports.

events.title: Russia forced a Ukrainian soldier to make a propaganda video. His village refused to bury him.
events.summary: Russia has coerced thousands of Ukrainian prisoners to denounce their leaders and country in propaganda videos. The consequences can follow them home.

events.title: Yemen says it asked Trump for U.S. military support in fight against Houthis
events.summary: A senior official said Yemen is seeking help as the Iranian-backed rebels tighten their grip on its Red Sea coast, threatening to further disrupt global energy shipments.

events.title: U.S. says China trade truce extended by 2 months
events.summary: The agreement extends the suspension of some tariffs as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for a state visit.

events.title: Iran’s president strikes a defiant tone at U.N. after Trump threats
events.summary: Masoud Pezeshkian’s appearance at the General Assembly was the first time the leader of a country at war with the U.S. has addressed the world body.

events.title: Trump tells U.N. he could ‘annihilate’ Iran but expects a deal after the midterm elections
events.summary: In a speech to world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly, President Donald Trump defended the Iran conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country and drive it “into hell.”

events.title: Tehran warns of ‘new weapons’ as Trump weighs meeting with Iranian president
events.summary: Iran warned Monday it would use “new weapons with new capabilities” if the U.S. launched a fresh assault after President Donald Trump ramped up the rhetoric against Tehran over the weekend.

events.title: U.S. proposes AI alert system with China ahead of Trump-Xi summit
events.summary: The United States has proposed a new AI safety notification mechanism for President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to consider at their summit in Washington this week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday.

events.title: Three dead in Moscow as Ukraine launches massive drone attack while Russia votes
events.summary: The largest Ukrainian drone attack reported so far on the Moscow region killed two people ⁠and damaged part of an oil refinery in the capital, authorities said Sunday.

events.title: Princess Diana’s brother says King Charles ‘gaslit’ him in dispute over book claims
events.summary: Princess Diana’s brother, Charles Spencer, has accused King Charles of gaslighting him after Buckingham Palace pushed back at his claims about the monarch’s conduct.

events.title: Diana’s brother says Charles sounded ‘giddily elated’ after her death
events.summary: Buckingham Palace remains gripped in drama as excerpts of Princess Diana’s brother’s book continues to be dripped into the public domain, ahead of its official release next week.

events.title: Trump administration grants visas to top Iranian leaders to attend U.N. General Assembly
events.summary: The decision to grant Iranian leaders visas to travel to New York City for the annual meeting of global leaders comes seven months into the U.S. war with Iran.

events.title: King Charles issues fiery response to Princess Diana’s brother over claims in new book
events.summary: In a rare rebuke, Buckingham Palace issued a robust statement aimed at King Charles III’s former brother-in-law, Earl Charles Spencer, as he is set to release his bombshell memoir.

events.title: Australian athlete apologizes after winning race despite involuntary bowel movement
events.summary: “Looking back, I regret the decision to not have stepped off the track,” Hyrox competitor Joanna Wietrzyk said.

events.title: How Canada and the E.U. are teaming up to counter Trump
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg to lay out how middle powers might counteract Trump’s hostility.

events.title: New wild cat species is identified for first time in 100 years, researchers say
events.summary: Researchers say they’ve identified a new species of wild cat previously unknown to science. The Tilcayo tiger cat is smaller than a typical house cat and lives in the Bolivian cloud forest.
